# Assist

> Assist is a native, local-first Mac app with three primary workflows: full-screen screenshot capture and editing, voice-powered screen annotation, and clipboard history from the Mac notch.

Canonical product facts:

- Platform: macOS 14 Sonoma or later.
- Screenshots: press Control + Option to capture the full display. The original is saved locally before the optional quick editor appears.
- Screenshot editing: crop freely or to a fixed ratio, blur with three brush sizes, and add padding, rounded corners, a shadow, or a backdrop.
- Voice annotation: hold Option to draw over the screen and optionally speak; release Option to save the annotated screenshot.
- Voice privacy: optional WhisperKit transcription runs locally on Apple silicon after a one-time model download. Raw audio is held in memory only while transcription finishes and is never saved by Assist.
- Clipboard: Assist keeps recently copied text locally and shows it beside screenshots and annotations in a combined history.
- Reuse: copy or drag a saved item into another app, or delete it from Assist history.
- Storage: screenshots, annotations, copied text, and optional transcripts stay on the Mac unless the user deliberately sends them elsewhere.
- Pricing: one-time purchase for one Mac, with the available regional price shown on the website and at checkout. There is no recurring subscription.

## Primary feature pages

- [Screenshots](https://assistapp.dev/screenshots): capture the full display, then optionally crop, blur, or frame the locally saved screenshot.
- [Voice annotation](https://assistapp.dev/voice-annotation): draw over the Mac screen, speak, and save the annotation with an optional local transcript.
- [Clipboard](https://assistapp.dev/clipboard): keep copied text beside screenshots in local history for filtering, copying, dragging, or deletion.
